item.title: Don't expect spike in arrests after B.C. ends drug decriminalization: police chief
item.description: The chief of Victoria's police department supports ending drug decriminalization in British Columbia, but says she doesn't expect to see a spike in arrests once the program ends this month, since it was already wound back 20 months ago.

item.description: Ryan Kempton, one of three men charged in connection to November 2023 abduction in Bradford, handed two-year jail term by Superior Court judge

item.title: Quebec economy minister considering bid to replace departing François Legault
item.description: MONTREAL — One day after Quebec Premier François Legault said he would resign ahead of the October election, at least one high-profile minister has come out publicly to say she is considering a bid to replace him.

item.title: Carney meets with Chinese President Xi Jinping
item.description: BEIJING — Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Xi welcomed Carney and his delegation to China.

item.title: Federal privacy commissioner looking into sexualized deepfakes on X platform
item.description: OTTAWA — The federal privacy commissioner will investigate the proliferation of sexualized deepfakes created by artificial intelligence chatbot Grok and shared on X.

item.title: Leah Gazan backs Avi Lewis, becomes first NDP MP to endorse a leadership candidate
item.description: OTTAWA — Manitoba NDP MP Leah Gazan is formally endorsing documentarian Avi Lewis for the party's leadership, making her the first sitting MP to officially back a candidate.

item.title: Heritage minister says hockey romance 'Heated Rivalry' is a Cancon triumph
item.description: OTTAWA — The Canadian TV show "Heated Rivalry" is winning fans all around the world — including Culture Minister Marc Miller, who calls the show a Cancon triumph.

item.title: Ontario proposes to pause rule that lets cities require affordable housing units
item.description: TORONTO — Ontario is proposing to temporarily ban three major cities from requiring a certain percentage of affordable units in new buildings near transit stations, citing a downturn in the housing market.

item.title: A South Korean court sentences Yoon to 5 years in prison on charges related to martial law decree
item.description: SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — A South Korean court sentenced former President Yoon Suk Yeol to five years in prison Friday on some charges related to his imposition of martial law.
